newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly lower late Friday in lackluster trade, still pressured by some technical selling after prices earlier failed to breach resistance, market sources said.
At 1430 EDT, July eased 0.7 cent to $2.214 per million British thermal units. August was 2.3 cents lower at $2.21. Most other deferreds were steady to down 1.8 cents.

"All the bullish news is in the market -- we know about the (hot) weather and we still can't move up. Yesterday I was bullish, but I'm not seeing any confirmation today and I'm getting a little skeptical," said one Texas-based trader.

Most agreed the first heat of the season in the Midwest and Northeast helped trigger this week's rally, but with forecasts for more moderate weather there by midweek next week, traders said higher levels were difficult to sustain.

Chart traders said technical selling kicked in early when July failed to get through $2.25, setting the stage for a possible double top and minor reversal today if the market closes lower. Next resistance in July was along a down trendline in the $2.28 area and then at the recent highs between $2.36 and $2.37. Support was seen at $2.151, a possible double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In the news, El Paso Natural Gas Co's Blanco gas plant in the San Juan Basin was expected to be back this weekend. On Friday and Saturday, 240 mmcfd will still be cut but on Sunday operations will return to normal. The Blanco plant normally processes about one bcfd.

In the weekend cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed a few cents early, then slipped back to finish only slightly higher in the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly at about $2.05. New York city gate gas was quoted up slightly in the high-$2.40s on the first heat in the area.
NYMEX said 30,086 contracts traded by 1400 EDT.
On KCBT, July was still down one-half cent at $2.085, with deferreds steady to 4.5 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed 0.2 cent to 12.9 cents (NYMEX premium).
